The 2023 disclosure was a high-level statement that such failure 'could harm our business.' The introduction of specific consequences (dissatisfaction, contractual liabilities) provides more detailed substance regarding the nature of the risk exposure.

peer_results.rationale: Retrieved candidates concern gray market sales control (amd_2024_1A_D021) and manufacturing divestiture risks (amd_2024_1A_D097). Neither addresses product lifecycle management, technological adaptation, or maintaining customer satisfaction through lifecycle oversight, which are the core subjects of the target disclosure.

Retrieved candidates focus on strategic transaction risks (intc_2024_1A_D035) and AI-specific legal/reputational risks (intc_2024_1A_D017). These do not cover the general operational risk of managing product and service lifecycles to prevent customer dissatisfaction or financial harm as described in the target.

Retrieved candidates address ESG goal failures (mu_2024_1A_D040) and general AI adoption uncertainties (mu_2024_1A_D037). While AI risks touch on implementation costs, they do not equate to the specific business driver risk of managing product/service lifecycles to ensure customer satisfaction and avoid contractual liabilities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks of failing to adapt to industry and market changes
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA's accelerated computing platforms face rapid technological and customer requirement changes, creating a risk that failure to identify these changes, adapt strategies, or maintain product compatibility may adversely impact financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA disclose risks related to the management of product lifecycles and the need to adapt to rapid technological changes. AVGO specifically warns that failure to manage these lifecycles could harm the business. NVDA frames this as a risk of failing to meet evolving industry needs and explicitly lists 'manage product and software lifecycles to maintain customer and end-user satisfaction' as a critical operational requirement to avoid adverse financial impacts.

peer_results.rationale: Retrieved candidates discuss customer vertical integration and the risk of customers developing their own IC products or using competitors (qcom_2024_1A_D030, qcom_2024_1A_D075). This is a competitive/customer behavior risk, distinct from the internal operational risk of managing one's own product and service lifecycles.
